transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in to see me?

Hello. My wife and son really pushed me to come get evaluated because they are worried about me. My wife says I’ve been acting all over the place at work and at home, like I can’t control what I’m doing or keep it appropriate to what’s going on.
Have you ever had a similar episode before, especially one with very high energy, little need for sleep, or feeling unusually grand, or any past episodes of depression?

No, I've never experienced anything like that before—no periods of high energy, grandiosity, or depression. I've always been pretty steady until about a year ago when they changed the inventory system at my job. This is the first time I've ever struggled like this.
When did these changes in your behavior first start, and have they been continuous for more than a month or did they come and go?

The gradual decline in how I think and handle things started about a year ago when the new system was rolled out at work. But this jumbled and inappropriate behavior has been happening continuously for about the last six months now. It hasn't come and gone; it's just been constant.
Have you ever had a head injury, seizure, stroke, brain infection, or any other medical problem that started around the time your symptoms began?
No, I've never had a head injury, seizure, stroke, or any kind of brain infection. I don't have any major medical problems like that, and my physical health has generally been fine.
Have you ever heard voices, seen things other people could not, or felt that others were spying on you, trying to harm you, or controlling your thoughts?

No, I don't hear voices, see things that aren't there, or feel like people are spying on me or trying to harm me. While I sometimes feel like I'm not in control of my own body or actions, I don't feel like someone else is controlling my thoughts.

Have you started, stopped, or changed any medications, alcohol, or drug use around the time these symptoms began, or had any new medical illness or abnormal lab results? This helps me tell whether the symptoms could be caused by a medical condition rather than a primary psychiatric illness.
No, I haven't changed or started any medications, and I don't use drugs or alcohol. I also haven't been diagnosed with any new medical conditions or had any abnormal lab results recently.
Have you noticed a clear decline in your work, self-care, or relationships over this time, such as becoming more withdrawn, less motivated, or having trouble taking care of yourself?

Yes, there has been a major decline in both areas. I went from running one of the steadiest stores in our district to getting formally written up for chaotic shifts and missed orders. At home, my wife and son say they can't even rely on me for basic things like paying bills on time or keeping simple plans because I get too mixed up.
Have you ever had any abnormal brain tests or neurological symptoms like seizures, confusion, memory loss, or a change in consciousness around the time these problems started?
No, I haven't had any abnormal brain tests, seizures, or changes in my consciousness. I have, however, felt very mixed up and disorganized in my thinking recently.
How old were you when these symptoms first started, and did they begin fairly suddenly or gradually over time?

I am 59 now, so I was 58 when these difficulties first started about a year ago. It was a very gradual process, starting with me slowly losing my ability to handle things at work after the new inventory system rolled out. Over the last six months, though, it has gotten much worse and my thoughts and actions have become severely jumbled.
Did your symptoms begin only after the age of 40 or 50, or did you have any similar problems much earlier in adulthood? Also, have they been steadily worsening rather than coming in episodes?

Yes, they only started about a year ago when I was 58, and I have never had any similar problems earlier in my life. It has been a steady, gradual decline that has gotten progressively worse over the last year, rather than coming and going in episodes.

Have you become more emotionally flat or withdrawn, or had trouble speaking clearly because your thoughts feel disorganized? I’m asking because that can help tell whether this is a primary psychotic disorder or something caused by a medical condition.

I don't really feel emotionally flat or withdrawn, but I definitely struggle to speak clearly because my thoughts get so disorganized. For example, if I try to explain a simple work schedule, I'll suddenly start talking about barcodes turning into patterns and my mouth can't get back to the point. People just stare at me like I'm speaking complete nonsense, even though it all connects in my head at the time.
Did you have any long-standing personality changes, odd beliefs, or social/work problems earlier in life before age 50, or did everything truly begin only in the last year?

No, everything truly began only within the last year after that new inventory system was rolled out. Before that, and all throughout my adulthood, I was highly reliable and successfully ran one of the steadiest stores in our district. I never had any issues with my thinking, behavior, or work performance before this started.
Have you had any fixed false beliefs, like being watched, followed, or specially chosen, or have you heard or seen things that other people do not?

No, I have never experienced anything like that—I don't hear or see things, and I've never felt like I was being watched or specially chosen. My main struggles are just that my thoughts get completely jumbled up when I try to speak, and my physical actions sometimes feel totally out of my control.

Have you noticed your memory, attention, or ability to learn new information getting worse over this time, or is the main problem just the disorganized thinking and behavior? This helps me tell whether this is more likely a brain-related condition or a primary psychotic disorder.

The main problem is definitely the disorganized thinking and behavior rather than a simple loss of memory. While I do get mixed up with complex tasks like paying bills or managing schedules, the real struggle is that my thoughts get completely derailed, like talking about barcode patterns, and my physical actions—like pacing, freezing, or repeating words—feel totally out of my control.

Have you noticed any changes in your memory, attention, or ability to recognize people or places, or any new neurological symptoms like tremor, weakness, or trouble walking? These would suggest a medical cause rather than a primary schizophrenia-spectrum illness.

No, I haven't experienced things like tremors, weakness, trouble walking, or forgetting who people are. I still get very mixed up and sometimes freeze or pace like I mentioned before, but I don't have those other physical issues.
Have you had any recent brain imaging, blood tests, or a neurological evaluation to look for a medical cause of these symptoms, such as a brain tumor, dementia, or another brain disorder?

No, I haven't had any recent brain scans, blood tests, or neurological exams. This psychiatric evaluation with you is actually the first formal step I'm taking since my wife and son expressed their concerns about me.
Did your symptoms begin after a specific medical event or brain illness, such as a stroke, seizure, head injury, infection, or new medication, or did they start without any clear medical cause?

No, there wasn't any medical event, head injury, or new medication that started this. It all began gradually about a year ago, coinciding with a very stressful time at work when my long-time regional manager retired and a new inventory and scheduling system was introduced.

Before these symptoms started, did you ever have a neurological or brain illness such as a stroke, seizure, head injury, infection, or memory disorder, or did you have any brain scans or tests showing a problem?
No, I've never had any neurological illnesses, head injuries, seizures, or brain scans in my life. I have never experienced those kinds of medical issues before this all started.
Have you ever had a brain scan or neurological exam that showed a problem, or any evidence that these symptoms started because of a medical or brain illness?
No, I've never had a brain scan or a neurological exam in my life. I'm also not aware of any medical or brain illness that could be causing these symptoms.

Did you have any similar symptoms earlier in adulthood, or did these problems only begin after age 50 and steadily worsen over time? Also, have you ever had any periods where the symptoms completely went away and then returned?

No, I never had any issues like this earlier in my adulthood; it all started about a year ago when I was 58. It has been a continuous, gradual decline without any breaks or periods where things went back to normal. Especially over the last six months, it has gotten steadily worse and feels completely off the rails.

Have you ever had a neurological exam or brain scan that showed a problem, or any signs like memory loss, confusion, seizures, tremor, or trouble walking? This helps tell whether the symptoms are more likely due to a medical brain condition rather than schizophrenia.
I have never had a brain scan or a neurological exam. I also haven't experienced any seizures, tremors, or trouble walking.

Did the symptoms start suddenly over days to weeks, or have they been slowly worsening over months to years? Also, have you had any noticeable memory loss or confusion outside of the disorganized speech and behavior?

They didn't start suddenly; it has been a slow, gradual decline over the past year since the new inventory system rolled out, getting really off the rails over the last six months. I don't have actual memory loss where I'm forgetting things, but rather my thoughts and actions get extremely jumbled and disorganized. It is more about feeling highly confused and out of control in the moment than forgetting who or where I am.

Did you have a brain scan or any medical workup before age 50 that showed a brain or neurological problem, or has this been a completely new illness that started only in the last year with no prior history?

No, I never had any brain scans, neurological workups, or issues like this before age 50. This is a completely new illness that only started about a year ago when I was 58, following some major changes and intense stress at my retail job. Over the last six months, it has gotten much worse and my thoughts and actions have become severely jumbled.

Has anyone in your family ever had schizophrenia, psychosis, or similar long-term mental health problems? Also, have you ever had any earlier episodes of unusual thinking or behavior, even if they were mild or brief?

I am not aware of anyone in my family having those kinds of mental health issues. I have also never experienced anything like this before this past year, as I was always able to handle my life and work reliably until recently.
Did these symptoms begin only after a medical illness, head injury, stroke, seizure, or new medication, or did they start on their own without any clear physical cause?

No, they started completely on their own, without any head injury, stroke, seizure, medical illness, or new medication. They just seemed to build up gradually after the stress of the new inventory and scheduling system was introduced at my job about a year ago.

Did you have any psychiatric symptoms before age 50, or has this been a completely new problem that started only in the last year and steadily worsened? Also, has anyone ever found a medical or neurological cause for these changes?

No, I never had any psychiatric symptoms before this; it is a completely new problem that started about a year ago when I was 58 and has gotten steadily worse, especially over the last six months. No medical or neurological cause has ever been found, which is exactly why my family pushed for this psychiatric evaluation.
Did your symptoms begin before age 40, or did they only start later in life after age 40? Also, have they been steadily present for at least 6 months without another medical cause being found?

No, my symptoms only started about a year ago when I was 58, which is well after age 40. These severe, jumbled thoughts and behaviors have been steadily present and worsening for the past six months now. We haven't found any other medical cause for what is going on with me.

Did you ever have any similar symptoms earlier in life, especially before age 40, or is this the first time anything like this has ever happened? Also, did the problems start only in later adulthood and keep steadily worsening without clear episodes in between?

No, I never had anything like this before in my life, definitely not before age 40—I was always completely normal and reliable. It only started at age 58 with the new inventory system, and it has just steadily gotten worse over the last six months without any breaks or episodes. Sometimes I lose my train of thought trying to explain it, but yes, it’s just been one long, constant decline.
Have you had any recent brain imaging or a medical evaluation for conditions like dementia, a tumor, or another brain disorder that could explain these new symptoms?

No, I haven't had any recent brain imaging or medical tests for conditions like dementia or a tumor. This psychiatric evaluation with you is actually the first step I'm taking after my family pushed me to get some help.
Have you had any recent medical tests, such as blood work or a brain scan, that found a physical brain problem or another medical cause for these changes?

No, I haven't had any recent blood tests, brain scans, or other medical workups done for these issues yet. This evaluation with you is really the first step we've taken to figure out what is going on.
